profile.a: The author, writing in the first person as if NVIDIA's chief executive (a role-play for Strategy).
The course assessors; within the narrative, NVIDIA's board, investors and staff.
A reflection on 24 months leading NVIDIA after succeeding its founder, including the DeepSeek share-price shock.
May 2023 to mid-2025 in the narrative; the shock on 27 January 2025; handed in on 2 June 2025.
NVIDIA globally, competing in AI infrastructure with a Chinese challenger.
Succeeding a founder requires both continuity and renewal, and a competitor's breakthrough wiped $600bn off the company's value in a day.
Feigen Advisors' 'Unique Work of the CEO', Porter's five forces, Helmer's 7 Powers (three chosen) and Porter and Nohria's research on how CEOs use their time.

charts.title: The CEO's unique work, area by area

items.title: Vision, strategy and execution
items.text: Five forces review; deepen CUDA and data-centre leadership; decentralised teams with KPIs; talent density and top pay.

items.title: Capital
items.text: Acquisitions and stakes in AI start-ups instead of large buybacks; R&D on inference, compression and next-generation GPUs; a cash cushion inspired by Ford in 2008.

items.title: Governance
items.text: Scenario planning and rapid-response teams; new directors with AI ethics and quantum expertise; tighter risk standards.

items.title: Investors and stakeholders
items.text: Publicly praised DeepSeek as an 'excellent AI advancement', called a shareholder meeting, cited 93% data-centre growth and Blackwell.

items.title: Personal leadership
items.text: Humility as a founder's successor; stakeholder mapping, scenario planning and an advisory circle on AI policy and security.
